items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I heard Coltrane live. I guess I would like to revisit that because it was way over my head when I heard it.

ctx.x: Oh I would have like to have heard Jelly Roll live. That would be great. I found that, you know when I started listening I was listening to only the avante garde or what was considered the avante garde then. And now there is some traditional jazz, or the early classics, and I still don’t feel like I understand and know how they are — I mean they give me a lot of joy to listen to Jelly Roll or the Hot Fives. And that’s just as big a mystery to me as the Art Ensemble was when I first started listening to the Art…

curious about what’s going to happen basically than what’s already happened. I would have like to have heard Charlie Parker live. That would have been great. I think I heard Charlie Parker when I was about two or three, on the radio. I think that was really like my first early memory of hearing a saxophone solo. And as much as I can recapture it now, I think it must have been Bird. I can’t imagine who else it would have been. I heard Coltrane live.
